app.name: GazaBridge
nav.not_available: Not available in this build yet
home.intro: A secure desktop workspace for exploring, converting, migrating and synchronizing data between PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, SQLite and common file formats. Everything runs locally; no account or cloud service is required.
home.safety_body: Credentials are kept in your operating system's secure store, never in GazaBridge's own files. Lossy conversions always require your explicit approval, and destructive jobs require a Dry Run first.
connections.title: Connections
connections.empty_body: Creating and editing connections is not available in this build yet. Saved connections will appear here.
connections.catalogue_intro: Supported products and what GazaBridge knows about them. A product is only marked Production Ready after the connector contract suite has passed against its tested versions.
connections.connector_missing: Connector not included in this build
logs.title: Logs
logs.empty: No log entries match the current filter.
logs.redaction_note: Secrets are redacted before log lines are written. Record data is never logged.
settings.title: Settings
settings.row_limit_help: Data views never load an unbounded result. Between 1 and 10,000 rows.
settings.telemetry_body: GazaBridge does not collect telemetry. Nothing about your connections, databases, queries or data leaves this computer unless you run a job that sends it to a target you configured.
connections.delete_body: The saved connection and its stored password are removed. Your database is not touched.
connections.paste_help: Paste a postgres://, mongodb://, mongodb+srv://, mysql:// or sqlite: URI. The password is moved to secure storage and removed from the saved settings.
editor.create_if_missing: Create the file if it does not exist
editor.name: Name
editor.uri_help: Hosts, options and SRV records are taken from the URI. A password in the URI is moved to secure storage.
explorer.blocked_no_key: Editing is off: this object has no primary key, so a record cannot be identified safely.
explorer.blocked_not_writable: Editing is off: records of this kind of object cannot be changed (for example a view).
explorer.blocked_read_only: Editing is off: this connection is read-only.
explorer.blocked_unsupported: Editing is off: this connector does not support updates.
explorer.conflict: This record was changed since you loaded it. Saving is blocked so the other change is not overwritten; refresh and edit again.
explorer.delete_body: This permanently deletes the record from the database. It is refused if the record changed since you loaded it.
explorer.editor_help: Typed JSON: values such as {"$oid": …}, {"$date": …} and {"$numberDecimal": …} keep their exact type. Remove a field to unset it (documents only).
explorer.missing_hint: Field is missing from this document (not the same as null)
explorer.no_connections: Add a connection first, then browse its databases here.
explorer.pick_object: Pick a table, view or collection in the tree.
explorer.value_help: Values are typed JSON: 42, true, "text", {"$oid": "…"}. Anything that is not valid JSON is matched as text.
query.confirm_body: This cannot be undone from GazaBridge. Run it only if you have a backup or are sure.
query.explain_analyze_help: Runs the query to measure it. On PostgreSQL it runs inside a transaction that is always rolled back.
query.no_results: Run a query to see results here.
query.params_help: Typed JSON per line: 42, "text", {"$date": "…"}. Text that is not JSON is sent as a string. Values are always bound, never pasted into the SQL.
query.risk_delete: DELETE without WHERE removes every row of the table.
query.risk_drop: DROP permanently removes a database object.
query.risk_out: $out / $merge writes into a collection and can replace its contents.
query.risk_truncate: TRUNCATE removes every row of the table.
query.risk_unknown: This query may change data in bulk.
query.risk_update: UPDATE without WHERE changes every row of the table.
query.truncated: More rows exist than the limit
transfer.cancelled: Cancelled. A partial export file is never left behind; records already imported stay.
transfer.csv_columns_help: Leave empty to use the query's Project, else the table's columns or the top-level fields found in a sample of the collection.
transfer.csv_ignore: Leave out fields that are not columns (they are listed afterwards)
transfer.csv_loss: CSV is text: nested values are written as JSON, and empty cells cannot tell a missing field from an empty string. Use JSON or BSON to keep types.
transfer.flavor_help: Typed JSON keeps every value exactly. MongoDB relaxed JSON matches mongoexport/mongoimport; canonical JSON and BSON also keep 32-bit vs 64-bit integers.
transfer.malformed_count: Malformed records skipped or set aside
transfer.malformed_quarantine: Set aside in a separate file
transfer.replace_question: A file with this name already exists. Replace it?
transfer.stop_on_error: Stop when the database rejects a record
editor.connection_string_help: Paste a mongodb://, mongodb+srv://, postgres:// or mysql:// link. Everything else is filled in from it.
editor.connection_string_replace: Paste a connection string to replace these settings, or change them under Advanced connection options.
editor.password_moved: the password will be kept in the system keychain, not in GazaBridge's files
explorer.toggle_panel: Show or hide the object list
explorer.blocked_projected: Editing is off while only some fields are shown (Project). Clear Project to edit.
transfer.current_query: Only the results of the current query
transfer.no_query: No filter or query is applied in the viewer.
transfer.sort_note: The export holds exactly what the query shows: its filter, Project, Sort, Skip and Limit.
agg.help: Each stage works on the output of the one before it. Preview shows up to 20 documents.
agg.title: Aggregations
qb.any_help: at least one condition must match
qb.no_conditions: No conditions: every document matches. Add a condition or a group.
qb.too_complex: This query uses parts the builder cannot show; keep editing it as text.
settings.tree_counts: Show document counts in the Explorer tree
settings.tree_counts_help: Counts are estimates read from collection metadata, so they are instant and do not scan data, even on large production databases.
qb.sort_help: first key wins; later keys break ties
qb.find_field: Find a field, or type a name and press Enter
qb.no_field_match: No field matches; press Enter to add it anyway.
qb.showing_only: Only the chosen fields are shown (and _id).
qb.paging_help: Skip jumps over the first documents; Limit caps how many are shown.
qb.err_filter_doc: The filter must be a document, e.g. { status: "active" }.
qb.err_project: Fields: use 1 to show a field or 0 to hide it, not both (except _id: 0).
qb.err_sort: Sort: use 1 for ascending or -1 for descending, e.g. { createdAt: -1 }.
explorer.open_connection: Open a connection on the left to browse its databases.
transfer.xlsx_loss: Excel keeps numbers and text; nested values are written as JSON and dates as text. A sheet holds up to 1,048,576 rows. Use JSON or BSON to keep types.
mig.title: Copy and convert
mig.intro: Copy MongoDB collections to another MongoDB, convert them to PostgreSQL tables, or turn PostgreSQL tables into MongoDB documents. You can pause, resume after closing the app, and nothing is written before you review the plan.
mig.no_connections: The connections could not be loaded.
mig.pick_db_first: Choose a database to see its collections.
mig.target_db_help: Empty: the same name as the source database. A new name creates the database.
mig.existing_title: If the target already has data
mig.ex_skip: Keep them, copy only new documents
mig.ex_skip_help: Documents or rows whose key already exists are left as they are. Safe to run again.
mig.ex_update: Replace what has the same key
mig.ex_update_help: The source version wins; other target data stays.
mig.ex_fail: Stop if a document already exists
mig.ex_fail_help: For copying into empty collections or tables only.
mig.ex_replace_help: Drops the target collection or tables and their data, then copies. You will be asked to confirm.
mig.copy_indexes: Copy indexes (after the data, with the same options)
mig.err_quarantine: Save them to a file and continue
mig.advanced_help: Lower the batch size or set a limit to spare a busy production server.
mig.review_help: Reads counts and indexes only; nothing is written.
mig.statements: Commands that will run on the target
mig.destructive_title: This will delete existing data in the target.
mig.type_to_confirm: To confirm, type the target database name:
mig.resume_help: Resuming continues from the last saved point without copying anything twice.
mig.target_schema_help: Tables are created in this schema (it is created if missing). Each collection becomes a table with the same name.
mig.dm_flatten_help: address.city → address_city. Arrays stay JSONB. Fields outside the plan go to _extra, nothing is lost.
mig.dm_normalize_help: Like columns per field, and each array becomes a table linked by _parent_id (with a foreign key).
mig.dm_jsonb_help: _id plus the whole document in doc. Exact and simple; query it with ->> in SQL.
mig.dm_hybrid_help: Top-level simple fields as columns for fast queries, plus the whole document in _doc.
mig.tm_reference_help: The primary key becomes _id; foreign keys stay as values that reference other documents.
mig.tm_embed_help: Rows of a selected table that reference another selected table go inside its documents as an array.
mig.dry_run_note: Nothing was written, created or deleted. The numbers show what a copy would do: copied = new, already there = kept, replaced = updated, rejected = would fail (see Activity).
mig.check_help: Counts are quick. Every key confirms each document or row arrived. Deep check also compares content, chunk by chunk with checksums, and names the first differing field. Key and deep checks read both sides completely.
bk.title: Backups
bk.intro: Back up collections and tables, check a backup against its checksums, and restore it into the same or another connection, database or schema. Nothing is written before you review the restore.
bk.m_gazabridge_help: No tool needed. Exact BSON for MongoDB, typed rows for PostgreSQL, with indexes, keys and SHA-256 checksums. Restores into another database or schema.
bk.m_native_help: The database's own tool (an archive restorable outside GazaBridge too). The password goes through a private temporary file, never the command line.
bk.label: Name (optional)
bk.check_help: Verifies the files' checksums and looks at the target; nothing is written.
bk.type_to_confirm: To confirm, type the target name:
mig.backup_first: Back up the target before deleting it
mig.backup_at: Backup of the target before it was deleted:
pw.title: Password needed
pw.remember: Save it in the macOS keychain again
